136	  the base component + design-token library every other `@gravity-ui/*` package
137	  builds on; without it components render unstyled. If `package.json` lacks it,
138	  stop and have the user install and configure it first (setup:

145	  rather than guessing.

153	  `blue-500`); never hand-write `dark:` overrides. Full token tables live in
154	  `references/theming.md`; the cross-cutting traps (partial brand overrides,
155	  scoped vs nested `ThemeProvider`, controls on a brand background) live in
156	  `rules/hallucination-traps.md`.

158	  peer-deps). It lives in each package's root README under "Required setup" —
159	  read it once per package, do not rely on memory.

164	already implied by the rules above; this section exists as an explicit
165	stop-sign. If you are about to do any of these, stop and re-ground.

168	  `<input>`/`<button>`, or look-alike component libs. Use the `@gravity-ui/*`
169	  package the task needs.

175	  serves the newest major, which may differ from the installed one and have a
176	  different API. The versioned online fallback is the major-line URL
177	  (`/llms/<pkg>/<major>/llms.txt`); below that, go LOCAL.

179	  selection, focus, links and contrast on the default accent — a mismatched
180	  UI. Override the full brand token set, on each theme you support.
181	- **Do not override internal markup with `[class*='…']` / ID selectors.**
182	  That's written against one DOM structure and breaks silently when the
183	  component changes. Climb the customization ladder
184	  (global token → component CSS API → narrow flagged hack) before ever
185	  touching structure.

188

191	- `references/package-routing.md` — offline snapshot of the ecosystem catalog
192	  (`gravity-ui.com/llms.txt`), refreshed each skill release. Used as the
193	  offline fallback in Step 0.
194	- `references/theming.md` — verbatim copy of uikit's `docs/theming.md`:

196	  themes, `uikit-themer`. The bundled copy may lag — read
197	  `node_modules/@gravity-ui/uikit/build/docs/guides/theming.md` for the
198	  version-matched file.
199	- `references/layout.md` — verbatim copy of uikit's `docs/layout.md`:
200	  spacing scale (`--g-spacing-*`), `Flex`/`Box`, `Row`/`Col`/`Container`
201	  grid, breakpoints, `useLayoutContext`.
202	- `references/icons.md` — finding an icon by image
203	  (`scripts/icon-image-search.sh`) or on gravity-ui.com/icons; the
204	  object-vs-string rendering rule.
205	- `rules/hallucination-traps.md` — Incorrect/Correct pairs for the most
206	  commonly invented APIs: typography variants (`header-3..6` don't exist, no
207	  `Heading`), the flex contract (`min-width:0`, who shrinks), theming traps
208	  (partial brand overrides, scoped vs nested `ThemeProvider`, customization
209	  ladder), `Button view` not `variant`, `Icon data` not `name`. Per-component
210	  traps live in each package's `dist/docs`, not here.

2	
3	## Page constructor
4	
5	`Page-constructor` is a library for rendering web pages or their parts based on `JSON` data (support for `YAML` format is to be added later).
6	
7	When creating pages, component-based approach is used: a page is built using a set of ready-made blocks that can be placed in any order. Each block has a certain type and set of input data parameters.
8	
9	For the format of input data and list of available blocks, see the [documentation](https://preview.gravity-ui.com/page-constructor/?path=/docs/documentation-blocks--docs).
10	
11	## Install
12	
13	```shell
14	npm install @gravity-ui/page-constructor
15	```
16	
17	## Quick start
18	
19	First, we need a React project and some kind of server. For example, you can create a React project using Vite and an Express server, or you can create Next.js application - it will have a client and server side at once.
20	
21	Install the required dependencies:
22	
23	```shell
24	npm install @gravity-ui/page-constructor @diplodoc/transform @gravity-ui/uikit
25	```
26	
27	Insert the `Page Constructor` to the page. To work correctly, it must be wrapped in a `PageConstructorProvider`:
28	
29	```tsx
30	import {PageConstructor, PageConstructorProvider} from '@gravity-ui/page-constructor';
31	import '@gravity-ui/page-constructor/styles/styles.scss';
32	
33	const App = () => {
34	  const content = {
35	    blocks: [
36	      {
37	        type: 'header-block',
38	        title: 'Hello world',
39	        background: {color: '#f0f0f0'},
40	        description:
41	          '**Congratulations!** Have you built a [page-constructor](https://github.com/gravity-ui/page-constructor) into your website',
42	      },
43	    ],
44	  };
45	
46	  return (
47	    <PageConstructorProvider>
48	      <PageConstructor content={content} />
49	    </PageConstructorProvider>
50	  );
51	};
52	
53	export default App;
54	```
55	
56	This was the simplest example of a connection. In order for YFM markup to work, you need to process content on the server and receive it on the client.
57	
58	If your server is a separate application, then you need to install page-constructor:
59	
60	```shell
61	npm install @gravity-ui/page-constructor
62	```
63	
64	To process YFM in all base blocks, call the `contentTransformer` and pass the content and options there:
65	
66	```ts
67	const express = require('express');
68	const app = express();
69	const {contentTransformer} = require('@gravity-ui/page-constructor/server');
70	
71	const content = {
72	  blocks: [
73	    {
74	      type: 'header-block',
75	      title: 'Hello world',
76	      background: {color: '#f0f0f0'},
77	      description:
78	        '**Congratulations!** Have you built a [page-constructor](https://github.com/gravity-ui/page-constructor) into your website',
79	    },
80	  ],
81	};
82	
83	app.get('/content', (req, res) => {
84	  res.send({content: contentTransformer({content, options: {lang: 'en'}})});
85	});
86	
87	app.listen(3000);
88	```

91	
92	```tsx

94	import '@gravity-ui/page-constructor/styles/styles.scss';
95	import {useEffect, useState} from 'react';
96	
97	const App = () => {
98	  const [content, setContent] = useState();
99	
100	  useEffect(() => {
101	    (async () => {
102	      const response = await fetch('http://localhost:3000/content').then((r) => r.json());
103	      setContent(response.content);
104	    })();
105	  }, []);

384	### Analytics
385	
386	#### Init
387	
388	To start using analytics, pass a handler to the constructor. The handler must be created on the project side. It receives three classes of events:
389	
390	- **Default events** are generic Page Constructor events generated for button, link, navigation, and control interactions. Set `autoEvents.enabled` to `true` to emit them.
391	- **Extended events** are registered events supplied by a composing library. The presence of `autoEvents.extendedEvents` enables them independently of `enabled` and optionally adds a prefix and counter.
392	- **Custom events** are supplied by consumers through `analyticsEvents`. The auto-events configuration does not change them.
393	
394	The object form is the preferred configuration:
395	
396	```ts
397	function sendEvents(events: MyEventType []) {
398	  ...
399	}
400	
401	<PageConstructorProvider
402	    ...
403	
404	    analytics={{
405	        sendEvents,
406	        autoEvents: {
407	            enabled: true,
408	            extendedEvents: {
409	                prefix: 'LIBRARY_',
410	                counter: 'secondary',
411	            },
412	        },
413	    }}
414	
415	    ...
416	/>
417	```
418	
419	```ts
420	type ExtendedEventsConfig = {
421	  prefix?: string;
422	  counter?: string;
423	};
424	
425	type AutoEventsConfig = {
426	  enabled: boolean;
427	  extendedEvents?: ExtendedEventsConfig;
428	};
429	```
430	
431	The legacy boolean form remains supported for backward compatibility: `true` is equivalent to `{enabled: true}`, and `false` is equivalent to `{enabled: false}`. If `autoEvents` is omitted, both default and extended events are disabled. An `extendedEvents` object enables supplied extended events even when `enabled` is `false`.
432	
433	Extended events must have `type: 'extended-event'`. Their prefix is concatenated exactly as configured, without changing case, separators, or whitespace. If `counter` is set, it defines `counters.include` for the extended event:
434	
435	```ts
436	// Supplied event
437	{name: 'REGISTERED_CLICK', type: 'extended-event'}
438	
439	// Event received by sendEvents with the configuration above
440	{
441	  name: 'LIBRARY_REGISTERED_CLICK',
442	  type: 'extended-event',
443	  counters: {include: ['secondary']},
444	}
445	```
446	
447	Events are sent in this order: the generated default event first (when enabled), followed by supplied extended and custom events in their original order. Extended events are omitted when `extendedEvents` is not configured. Any interaction-specific additional context is merged into every emitted event last.
448	
449	An event object has only one required field - `name`. It also has predefined fields, which serve to help manage complex logic. For example, `counter.include` can help to send event in a particular counter if several analytics systems are used in a project.
450	
451	```ts
452	type AnalyticsEvent<T = {}> = T & {
453	  name: string;
454	  type?: string;
455	  counters?: AnalyticsCounters;
456	  context?: string;
457	};
458	```
459	
460	It is possible to configure an event type needed for a project.
461	
462	```ts
463	type MyEventType = AnalyticsEvent<{
464	  [key: string]?: string; // only a 'string' type is supported
465	}>;
466	```

468	#### Counter selector
469	
470	It is possible to configure an event to which an analytics system to sent.
471	
472	```ts
473	type AnalyticsCounters = {
474	  include?: string[]; // array of analytics counter ids that will be applied
475	  exclude?: string[]; // array of analytics counter ids that will not be applied
476	};
477	```
478	
479	#### context parameter
480	
481	Pass `context` value to define place in a project where an event is fired.
482	
483	Use selector below or create logic that serves project needs.
484	
485	```ts
486	// analyticsHandler.ts
487	if (isCounterAllowed(counterName, counters)) {
488	  analyticsCounter.reachGoal(counterName, name, parameters);
489	}
490	```

492	#### Reserved event types
493	
494	Several predefined event types are used to mark automatically configured events. Use the types to filter default events, for example.
495	
496	```ts
497	enum PredefinedEventTypes {
498	  Default = 'default-event', // default events which fire on every button click
499	  Extended = 'extended-event', // events supplied by a composing library
500	  Play = 'play', // React player event

652	
653	- Data-driven pages: render a `content` config of typed blocks with `PageConstructor` wrapped in `PageConstructorProvider`.
654	- Marketing, landing, and documentation pages assembled from prebuilt blocks (headers, media, cards, etc.).
655	- Server-side YFM processing of block text via the `@gravity-ui/page-constructor/server` utilities (`contentTransformer`, `fullTransform`).

665	
666	- **`PageConstructor` must be wrapped in `PageConstructorProvider`.** Rendering it bare breaks context (locale, theme, SSR, analytics).
667	- **The content prop is `content`, shaped `{blocks: [...]}`.** Each block object needs a `type` matching a known block plus its data fields; there is no `data`/`config` prop.
668	- **YFM in block text needs server processing.** Markdown-like fields render as plain text unless you run content through `contentTransformer`/`fullTransform` from `@gravity-ui/page-constructor/server`; `@diplodoc/transform` is a required peer dependency.
669	- **Import the SCSS styles.** Add `@gravity-ui/page-constructor/styles/styles.scss` (SCSS, not CSS); custom blocks import the same file to reuse mixins/variables.

7	When creating pages, component-based approach is used: a page is built using a set of ready-made blocks that can be placed in any order. Each block has a certain type and set of input data parameters.
8	
9	For the format of input data and list of available blocks, see the [documentation](https://preview.gravity-ui.com/page-constructor/?path=/docs/documentation-blocks--docs).
10

19	First, we need a React project and some kind of server. For example, you can create a React project using Vite and an Express server, or you can create Next.js application - it will have a client and server side at once.

31	import '@gravity-ui/page-constructor/styles/styles.scss';
32	
33	const App = () => {
34	  const content = {
35	    blocks: [
36	      {
37	        type: 'header-block',
38	        title: 'Hello world',
39	        background: {color: '#f0f0f0'},
40	        description:
41	          '**Congratulations!** Have you built a [page-constructor](https://github.com/gravity-ui/page-constructor) into your website',
42	      },
43	    ],
44	  };

46	  return (
47	    <PageConstructorProvider>
48	      <PageConstructor content={content} />
49	    </PageConstructorProvider>
50	  );
51	};
52	
53	export default App;
54	```

59	
60	```shell
61	npm install @gravity-ui/page-constructor

64	To process YFM in all base blocks, call the `contentTransformer` and pass the content and options there:

66	```ts

68	const app = express();
69	const {contentTransformer} = require('@gravity-ui/page-constructor/server');
70	
71	const content = {
72	  blocks: [

74	      type: 'header-block',
75	      title: 'Hello world',

94	import '@gravity-ui/page-constructor/styles/styles.scss';
95	import {useEffect, useState} from 'react';

332	### How to add a new block to the `page-constructor`
333	
334	1. In the `src/blocks` or `src/sub-blocks` directory, create a folder with the block or sub-block code.
335	
336	2. Add the block or sub-block name to enum `BlockType` or`SubBlockType` and describe its properties in the `src/models/constructor-items/blocks.ts` or `src/models/constructor-items/sub-blocks.ts` file in a similar way to the existing ones.

338	3. Add export for the block in the `src/blocks/index.ts` file and for the sub-block in the `src/sub-blocks/index.ts` file.
339	
340	4. Add a new component or block to mapping in `src/constructor-items.ts`.
341	
342	5. Add a validator for the new block:
343	
344	   - Add a `schema.ts` file to the block or sub-block directory. In this file, describe a parameter validator for the component in [`json-schema`](http://json-schema.org/) format.
345	   - Export it in the `schema/validators/blocks.ts` or `schema/validators/sub-blocks.ts` file.

349	7. In the block directory add storybook demo in `__stories__` folder. All demo content for story should be placed in `data.json` at story dir. The generic `Story` must accept the type of block props, otherwise incorrect block props will be displayed in Storybook.

384	### Analytics
385	
386	#### Init
387	
388	To start using analytics, pass a handler to the constructor. The handler must be created on the project side. It receives three classes of events:
389	
390	- **Default events** are generic Page Constructor events generated for button, link, navigation, and control interactions. Set `autoEvents.enabled` to `true` to emit them.
391	- **Extended events** are registered events supplied by a composing library. The presence of `autoEvents.extendedEvents` enables them independently of `enabled` and optionally adds a prefix and counter.
392	- **Custom events** are supplied by consumers through `analyticsEvents`. The auto-events configuration does not change them.
393	
394	The object form is the preferred configuration:
395	
396	```ts
397	function sendEvents(events: MyEventType []) {
398	  ...
399	}
400	
401	<PageConstructorProvider
402	    ...
403	
404	    analytics={{
405	        sendEvents,
406	        autoEvents: {
407	            enabled: true,
408	            extendedEvents: {
409	                prefix: 'LIBRARY_',
410	                counter: 'secondary',
411	            },
412	        },
413	    }}
414	
415	    ...
416	/>
417	```
418	
419	```ts
420	type ExtendedEventsConfig = {
421	  prefix?: string;
422	  counter?: string;
423	};
424	
425	type AutoEventsConfig = {
426	  enabled: boolean;
427	  extendedEvents?: ExtendedEventsConfig;
428	};
429	```
430	
431	The legacy boolean form remains supported for backward compatibility: `true` is equivalent to `{enabled: true}`, and `false` is equivalent to `{enabled: false}`. If `autoEvents` is omitted, both default and extended events are disabled. An `extendedEvents` object enables supplied extended events even when `enabled` is `false`.
432	
433	Extended events must have `type: 'extended-event'`. Their prefix is concatenated exactly as configured, without changing case, separators, or whitespace. If `counter` is set, it defines `counters.include` for the extended event:
434	
435	```ts
436	// Supplied event
437	{name: 'REGISTERED_CLICK', type: 'extended-event'}
438	
439	// Event received by sendEvents with the configuration above
440	{
441	  name: 'LIBRARY_REGISTERED_CLICK',
442	  type: 'extended-event',
443	  counters: {include: ['secondary']},
444	}
445	```
446	
447	Events are sent in this order: the generated default event first (when enabled), followed by supplied extended and custom events in their original order. Extended events are omitted when `extendedEvents` is not configured. Any interaction-specific additional context is merged into every emitted event last.
448	
449	An event object has only one required field - `name`. It also has predefined fields, which serve to help manage complex logic. For example, `counter.include` can help to send event in a particular counter if several analytics systems are used in a project.
450	
451	```ts
452	type AnalyticsEvent<T = {}> = T & {
453	  name: string;
454	  type?: string;
455	  counters?: AnalyticsCounters;
456	  context?: string;
457	};
458	```
459	
460	It is possible to configure an event type needed for a project.
461	
462	```ts
463	type MyEventType = AnalyticsEvent<{
464	  [key: string]?: string; // only a 'string' type is supported
465	}>;
466	```
467	
468	#### Counter selector
469	
470	It is possible to configure an event to which an analytics system to sent.
471	
472	```ts
473	type AnalyticsCounters = {
474	  include?: string[]; // array of analytics counter ids that will be applied
475	  exclude?: string[]; // array of analytics counter ids that will not be applied
476	};
477	```
478	
479	#### context parameter
480	
481	Pass `context` value to define place in a project where an event is fired.
482	
483	Use selector below or create logic that serves project needs.
484	
485	```ts
486	// analyticsHandler.ts
487	if (isCounterAllowed(counterName, counters)) {
488	  analyticsCounter.reachGoal(counterName, name, parameters);
489	}
490	```
491	
492	#### Reserved event types
493	
494	Several predefined event types are used to mark automatically configured events. Use the types to filter default events, for example.
495	
496	```ts
497	enum PredefinedEventTypes {
498	  Default = 'default-event', // default events which fire on every button click
499	  Extended = 'extended-event', // events supplied by a composing library
500	  Play = 'play', // React player event
501	  Stop = 'stop', // React player event
502	}
503	```

Vite externalizes node builtins; the `url` package installed in node_modules — does Vite resolve bare 'url' to the npm package instead of builtin? Actually the warning came from vite:resolve during transform. In build, rollup would resolve 'url' — Vite's resolver for client marks builtins as external only if not found? Not sure.
